findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a display-friendly config copy but then returns the raw config
findings.body: In `get_monitor_environment_context`, line 160 copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value (lines 161-162), but the returned dict at line 168 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the unmodified original) instead of the local `config` variable. The `schedule_type` translation is therefore computed and silently discarded, and the monitor context embedded in the occurrence event always contains the raw schedule type. This is carried over from the previous location in `mark_failed.py`, but since the module is being split out now is a good time to fix it (either return `config` or drop the dead copy).

findings.title: Public functions were renamed/moved but the PR contains no test updates
findings.body: This PR renames `mark_failed_threshold` to `try_incident_threshold` (now in `sentry.monitors.logic.incidents`) and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence` (now in `sentry.monitors.logic.incident_occurrence`), and moves the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` to `sentry.monitors.types`. No test files are changed in this PR. Any existing tests or callers that import these names from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` (e.g. the monitors logic tests that exercise `mark_failed_threshold`/`get_failure_reason`/`get_monitor_environment_context`) will now fail with ImportError, and the moved logic loses test coverage attribution. Before merging, the PR should either update the imports in the affected tests/callers or add `mark_failed_threshold = try_incident_threshold`-style aliases, and move/extend the corresponding tests alongside the moved code.

findings.title: get_failure_reason docstring examples do not match the produced strings and contain typos
findings.body: The docstring for `get_failure_reason` says it builds strings like "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "3 missed check-ins detected", but the code actually produces "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in check-ins detected" (the template appends "check-ins detected" to a list whose items already end in "check-in"), and the "3 missed check-ins detected" example cannot be produced at all since a single-status count yields "3 missed check-ins check-ins detected". The docstring also reads "humam readible" instead of "human readable". Since the function is being moved into its own module as a public helper (part of GH-80527 work), the docstring should be corrected to describe the actual output.
